subject: Re: Clarify invoicing ownership & pass-through language for marketplace connector
messages:
From: Sam Irani <sam.irani@bluelake.io>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@bluelake.io, finance@bluelake.io
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: Marketplace addendum invoicing & pass-through mapping

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the draft partner paper — we reviewed the addendum and had a couple of fast questions from the finance/procurement teams before we proceed to redlines:

1) Invoice ownership: your addendum references "Partner to invoice end customer and remit to Redwood" — we need clarity on whether BlueLake or Redwood issues the primary invoice to the end customer for marketplace transactions. Our accounting team needs the canonical owner for VAT and AR aging.

2) Pass-through fees & taxes: the draft allocates marketplace fees to BlueLake but references a "pass-through" waterfall without an audit trigger. Can you confirm what evidence Redwood will accept if BlueLake needs to pass charges back?

3) Audit window and retention: what records must BlueLake retain and for how long? Our procurement team is concerned about a broad audit right.

We attached the partner_paper_draft.pdf with highlighted sections. Could you propose explicit language for (1) invoice ownership and (2) pass-through evidence (types of documentation + time window)?

If helpful, happy to do a 30-min call this week — procurement is available Wed/Thu afternoons.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Irani
Head of Partnerships, BlueLake Systems
(Attachment: partner_paper_draft.pdf)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Irani <sam.irani@bluelake.io>
Cc: procurement@bluelake.io, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: Marketplace addendum invoicing & pass-through mapping

Sam — appreciate the quick review and concrete asks. Short answers up front, then I'll loop legal & ops with suggested language.

- Invoice ownership: Redwood is proposing to remain the primary biller for all hosted/marketplace invoices where we provide the service directly. For reseller flows where BlueLake resells under its own brand, we suggested partner-issued invoices. We can narrow this to a single rule for the connector: if BlueLake is the listed seller on the cloud marketplace order, BlueLake issues the invoice; otherwise Redwood invoices.

- Pass-through evidence: reasonable to require purchase/order confirmations, a copy of the end-customer invoice, and payment remittance details within a 12-month window. We can avoid a broad unlimited audit right and limit audits to once per 12 months unless there is a material dispute.

- Retention: propose 24 months minimum for invoice & remittance evidence tied to the transaction.

I'll push a short redline and sample clause to legal for sign-off and follow up with a clean paragraph you can drop into the addendum. Proposed 30-min slots: Wed 2:00pm PT or Thu 3:30pm PT — which works for procurement?

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Partnerships, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redlines_aditya_v1.docx)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: sam.irani@bluelake.io
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Quick Q: Marketplace addendum invoicing & pass-through mapping

Team — forwarding BlueLake's questions and my initial proposals. They want explicit, short language we can drop into the partner paper. High level items we need legal/ops alignment on: 

1) Invoice ownership rule: (A) Redwood invoices when Redwood is the seller-of-record; (B) Partner invoices when partner is seller-of-record on marketplace order. Is this acceptable? If not, state exceptions.

2) Pass-through evidence & audit: I propose we allow partner to submit (i) a copy of the end-customer invoice, (ii) remittance or bank trace showing payment to partner, and (iii) the original marketplace order confirmation. Limit audits to once per 12-month period and cap scope to financial reconciliation of disputed charges.

3) Retention/escrow trigger: legal preferred to avoid open-ended escrow obligations. Can we limit escrow or audit triggers to material breach of payment > $50k or repeated discrepancies over two consecutive quarters?

Attachments: proposed_clause_snippets.txt (short sample language), redlines_aditya_v1.docx (my tracked edits), and a quick invoice flow diagram on Drive: https://drive.redwoodinference.com/Shared/BlueLake/connector-invoice-flow-diagram.png

Quick asks:
- Laura: can you provide two short draft paragraphs (invoice ownership + pass-through evidence) we can send to BlueLake?
- Ben/Marissa: who will own ops verification for the remittance evidence if BlueLake provides it? We likely need a 48hr triage SLA.

Thanks — goal is to get legal-signed wording by Friday so we can present a small set of acceptable redlines to BlueLake on next week's call.

Aditya
(Attachment: proposed_clause_snippets.txt; redlines_aditya_v1.docx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Irani <sam.irani@bluelake.io>
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Quick Q: Marketplace addendum invoicing & pass-through mapping

Aditya — thanks for the summary. Attached are legal's clean redlines and two short paragraphs we can propose. High level legal positions below (tl;dr):

- Invoice ownership: agree with the simple seller-of-record rule. Proposed sentence: "For marketplace transactions, the party identified as the seller of record on the marketplace order shall be the issuing party for invoices to the end customer; taxes and duties shall be the responsibility of the issuing party unless otherwise agreed in writing."

- Pass-through evidence and audits: we will accept (i) a copy of the end-customer invoice, (ii) bank remittance showing payment to the partner, and (iii) the marketplace order/fulfillment record. Limit audit rights to one on-site/remote audit per 12-month period and only for one year of transaction history unless fraud is reasonably suspected.

- Escrow/cap: do not agree to an automatic escrow. If BlueLake requests escrow, condition it on a material unpaid balance > $75,000 and require prior written notice and opportunity to cure.

Operational asks: Ben/Marissa — if BlueLake provides remittance evidence, ops will validate that the invoice line items and amounts reconcile against our usage metering. We recommend a 72-hour window for ops to review remittance before accepting pass-through. If discrepancies > 2% of the invoice value are found, escalate to finance/legal.

I'll attach legal_redlines_clean.docx and the two paragraph snippets as text in the doc. Once Aditya confirms pricing/discount considerations with Sam, we can send these two paragraphs as an acceptable redline.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: legal_redlines_clean.docx)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Irani <sam.irani@bluelake.io>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 9 Oct 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Final: proposed connector addendum language & next steps

Sam — thanks for the patience. Legal and ops aligned on concise language we can put into the partner paper. Summary below (you can paste directly into the addendum):

1) Invoice ownership (text): "For marketplace transactions, the party identified as the seller of record on the marketplace order shall be the issuing party for invoices to the end customer; taxes and duties shall be the responsibility of the issuing party unless otherwise agreed in writing."

2) Pass-through evidence (text): "To effectuate any pass-through or chargeback, Partner shall provide (i) a copy of the end-customer invoice, (ii) proof of remittance or bank trace showing payment to Partner, and (iii) the marketplace order confirmation. Redwood reserves the right to request one audit (remote or on-site) per 12-month period limited to one year of transaction history unless reasonable grounds for fraud are identified."

3) Retention & escrow: Redwood proposes 24 months' retention for transactional records and will consider escrow only for material unpaid balances exceeding $75,000 after notice and cure.

Next steps:
- I uploaded the redlines and clause snippets to Drive (link above) and attached the final legal redlines for your records.
- If acceptable, please sign the addendum via DocuSign: https://docusign.com/rc/12345-connector-addendum
- We can still do a quick call Wed/Thu if you prefer a walkthrough; otherwise we'll expect a signed copy by Oct 16 to hit the billing go-live.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this piece.

Aditya Rao
Senior Partnerships, Redwood Inference

aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
